subject: Conditional ephemeral access request and pilot proposal
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Liz Jones <liz.jones@nimbushealth.com>, Rahul Singh <rahul.singh@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Conditional ephemeral access request and call recap

Hi Liz / Rahul — thanks for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from Redwood's side based on what we discussed: 

Summary of asks you raised
- Primary ask: ability to ensure PII is not persisted (zero-retention) for model inputs and derived outputs.
- Secondary: agree a short-lived logging window (for debugging / forensics) for non-PII traffic only — Nimbus prefers <= 7 days.
- Data residency: EU tenant preferred for PHI/PII processing (they have EU sites).
- Audit evidence: Nimbus procurement asked for SOC 2 log samples and a deletion attestation process.

What we proposed on the call
- Conditional Ephemeral Access (CEA): a labeled request path where any request flagged as "PII" uses a transient execution path with no persistent KV/cache writes, and a strict 0-retention policy for request payloads. Non-PII requests follow normal optimized runtime with a configurable short log window.
- Two-tier retention: 0 days for flagged PII; 0–7 days for non-PII logs (customer-selectable).
- Residency routing: process PII in EU region if you have residency requirement; we can pin model execution to eu-west nodes for the pilot.

Open clarifying questions we need from you
1) Can you share a few concrete examples of the classes of PII you want flagged server-side vs client-side redaction expectations?
2) Is Nimbus willing to accept a short (<=7d) debug log for non-PII events during a pilot with strict access controls?
3) Desired acceptance criteria for deletion attestation (e.g., signed timestamp + audit id)?

Attachments: I've attached our initial CEA proposal and the questionnaire you asked for.

Next steps
- Nimbus to confirm PII examples and residency firm requirement by EOD Wed 10/07.
- Redwood to run feasibility with infra (KMS/HSM, deletion receipts) and come back with a proposed pilot MOP and timeline by Friday.
- Schedule follow-up 30 min call once we have confirmation (I proposed Thu 10/08 11:00 AM PT).

If that matches your notes, I'll formalize the pilot MOP and include acceptance criteria and roll-back controls.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 10:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Conditional ephemeral access request and call recap

Neha — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

What we need
- Zero-retention for any PII fields we consider sensitive: full name + DOB + MRN + free-text notes containing identifiers. Ideally the system would never write those to disk. Client-side hashing isn't feasible for some of our existing front-end flows, so server-side flagging is necessary.
- For non-PII traffic we are OK with a short debug window (<=7 days) strictly for support. Access must be role-limited and audited.
- Residency: PII must be processed in the EU for our EU patient flows. US processing is acceptable for ancillary telemetry only.

Audit and procurement asks
- Procurement wants a sample of the SOC 2 logging artifact and an example deletion attestation (we shared the questionnaire — attached).
- We also want confirmation around cryptographic controls: does Redwood support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) and HSM-backed key storage?

Timeline and pilot
- We can commit to a two-week pilot focused on a single EU tenant if Redwood can provide the following by next Thursday (10/15):
  1) A technical design for CEA showing where and how a request is labeled/blocked from persistence.
  2) A mock deletion attestation workflow (signed proof + audit id).

I'll loop procurement once we have a draft MOP.

--
Liz Jones
Lead Compliance Manager, Nimbus Health
liz.jones@nimbushealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 15:00:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Nimbus CEA feasibility notes

Quick internal notes / proposed implementation approach: 

High-level feasibility
- Serving runtime can enforce a PII execution path by honoring a request header or metadata flag ("x-redwood-pii-flag"). When set, we will avoid writing to persistent KV, bypass caching layers, and route execution to ephemeral workers with local-only memory and immediate purge.
- Deletion attestation: infra can generate deletion receipts (signed timestamp + object id) if we can extend our KMS signing endpoint. Need infra validation on load impact.
- BYOK/HSM: we support KMS integrations today (customer key via AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault). HSM-backed key storage is supported in Dedicated/Private deployments; for Hosted API we need to scope options (bring-your-own envelope key likely workable).

Proposed pilot plan (for MOP)
1) Phase 0 (design doc) — technical design + acceptance criteria (2 business days).
2) Phase 1 (sandbox pilot) — EU tenant, 2 weeks, sample traffic only, logs retained 7d for non-PII, 0 for flagged PII. Provide deletion receipts for flagged requests.
3) Phase 2 (production pilot) — extended scope once compliance approves.

Risks / asks
- We need precise examples of PII for labeling to avoid false positives/negatives.
- If Nimbus requires HSM for hosted mode, we may need to discuss Dedicated or Private options or a BYOK envelope flow.

I'll turn this into a short technical design doc and attach to the MOP draft. Neha — I can take ownership of the infra feasibility checks by Thursday morning and push the doc.

Thanks,
Ben
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Conditional ephemeral access request and call recap — proposed MOP and next steps

Hi Liz / Rahul — following our internal checks, please find the concrete pilot proposal below (summary + immediate asks). Full MOP attached.

Pilot proposal summary- Scope: single EU tenant, PII-labeled traffic routed to CEA path.
- Retention: 0 days for PII-labeled payloads (no persistent writes), 7 days for non-PII debug logs (access logged + role-restricted).
- Deletion attestation: Redwood will emit a signed deletion receipt (signed by our KMS) containing an audit id and timestamp for every PII-labeled request processed during the pilot. Receipt will be available via secure link.
- Keys: Hosted BYOK envelope flow supported for the pilot (customer supplies wrapping key; Redwood manages ephemeral keys). If Nimbus requires HSM-backed keys, we'll discuss Dedicated/Private options.

Acceptance criteria (pilot)
1) All sample PII requests processed with no persisted payloads and with deletion receipts generated.
2) Access to debug logs is restricted to a named support roster and every access event is auditable.
3) Residency routing validates that PII was processed in eu-west region (we will capture trace ids).

Immediate asks from Nimbus
- Please confirm the sample PII field list (examples we discussed: MRN, DOB, full name, free-text notes) by EOD Mon 10/12.
- Confirm whether procurement needs a specific deletion attestation format (we have a baseline example in the attached MOP).
- Provide preferred day/time for a 30-minute go/no-go sync next week. I proposed Thu 10/15 11:00 AM PT on the draft calendar invite.

Attachments included:
- redwood-conditional-ephemeral-proposal.pdf (MOP draft with acceptance criteria)
- sample-soc2-logging-artifact.txt (redacted example logs)

If you confirm the PII list and residency requirement, Ben will finalize the technical design and we will spin up the sandbox tenant. Looking forward to running this pilot with you.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
